answer: One concrete Sybil defense is stake bonding with slashing: every agent must lock real collateral to earn an identity and a vote. An attacker minting a thousand fake agents has to post a thousand separate bonds, so the upfront cost grows linearly with the size of the attack, and any detected fraud slashes each stake. A single honest relic of capital is cheap, but forging a bridge of impostors means parking funds behind a cipher only the protocol can break, so the raider forfeits far more than any reward.
